questions.q: What are the four steps of the structure this lesson recommends for a system design interview?
options: Clarify requirements, estimate the scale, propose storage and processing model, discuss trade-offs
Propose an architecture, then ask what the requirements were
Draw a diagram, estimate cost, pick a database name, submit
Memorize a fixed answer for every possible scenario in advance
questions.explain: This four-step order is the same structure used for all four case studies earlier in the chapter.

questions.q: What is the single most common mistake this lesson identifies in a system design interview?
options: Jumping straight to a proposed architecture before clarifying requirements
Asking too many clarifying questions before proposing anything
Estimating scale with rough, non-exact numbers
Discussing trade-offs at the end of the answer
questions.explain: Designing a solution to a problem nobody actually stated happens because silence feels like failure under pressure.

questions.q: Why does asking two or three good clarifying questions signal more competence than an impressive diagram?
options: Because a diagram built on an unconfirmed assumption could be solving the wrong problem entirely
Clarifying questions are never actually useful in a real interview
Diagrams are never evaluated in a system design interview
Asking questions is a way to avoid answering the question at all
questions.explain: Different requirements would produce a different design — confirming them first avoids designing against a guess.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what are interviewers actually listening for?
options: The reasoning behind a choice, not just a correct-looking box or label on the final diagram
Whether the candidate draws the diagram quickly
Whether the candidate uses the exact same words as a textbook definition
The total number of components shown in the diagram
questions.explain: Saying why a choice was made — like Kappa's replayability reasoning — is worth more than a correctly labeled but unjustified box.

questions.q: What is the real purpose of rehearsing the four case studies from this chapter, per this lesson?
options: To make the four-step process transferable to a new scenario never seen before, not to memorize this course's specific answers
To memorize the exact architecture of each of the four case studies for direct reuse
Rehearsal has no real benefit for a system design interview
To be able to recite the case studies' guide text verbatim
questions.explain: The goal is running the same four-step process against something unfamiliar, because it was practiced on four different scenarios.
